This is a classic relative speed problem. We need to find the time when both trains have traveled the same distance from the starting station.

### Step 1: Calculate Train 1's Head Start Distance
The first train (T1) leaves at 2:00, and the second train (T2) leaves at 3:00. T1 has a head start of 1 hour.

*   Distance = Rate × Time
*   $D_{\text{head start}} = 60 \text{ km/h} \times 1 \text{ hour} = 60 \text{ km}$

At 3:00, T1 is 60 km ahead of T2. This is the distance T2 must close.

### Step 2: Calculate the Relative Speed
Since both trains are moving in the same direction, the speed at which T2 closes the gap is the difference between their speeds.

*   Relative Speed ($R_{\text{rel}}$) = $R_2 - R_1$
*   $R_{\text{rel}} = 90 \text{ km/h} - 60 \text{ km/h} = 30 \text{ km/h}$

### Step 3: Calculate the Time to Meet
We use the distance T2 needs to close (the head start) and the relative speed.

*   Time = Distance / Rate
*   $T_{\text{meet}} = 60 \text{ km} / 30 \text{ km/h} = 2 \text{ hours}$

This means it will take 2 hours for T2 to catch T1, starting from when T2 left the station (3:00).

### Step 4: Determine the Final Time
The meeting time is found by adding the elapsed time to Train 2's start time.

*   Meeting Time = 3:00 + 2 hours = 5:00
